content_html_sanitized:
Posted July 9, 2002
Exclusive to MarijuanaNews.com

Colin Davies hearing has been delayed until Thursday, and his supporters are not optimistic. It is clear that the police are going to extraordinary lengths to make him suffer.

As I reported last Friday, Colin was held in Strangeways Prison over the weekend because the prosecution appealed the court's order that he be released. He had been illegally charged with possession with intent to distribute after he had been ordered released on the same evidence on a charge of simple possession. In order for him to be held the police had to have " new evidence, " not simply escalate the charges based on the same evidence.
See

Now the police claim to have that " new evidence. " They say that they will introduce video surveillance tapes on Thursday that show him entering his own apartment the day before his arrest in violation of the terms of his bail. After being held in Strangeways Prison without bail for six months, he was finally released on bail on May 17th -- with some very bizarre conditions, one of which was that he could not go to his own apartment!

Unless there are extraordinary circumstances, such as a medical necessity, as was claimed for Colin's having been in his apartment when he was arrested, violation of any of the terms of the bail can result in his reimprisonment.

Yes, sometimes you really cannot go home again!

How did this happen?

In Britain, there is widespread use of closed circuit video cameras on the streets, supposedly to monitor for street crime. Presumably it was one of these, not a special camera set up to watch Colin's apartment, that caught the alleged proof of this violation of his bail.

While the cameras are hardly as ubiquitous as in Orwell's 1984, their use in this case shows that they can be used for purposes unrelated to public safety unless one believes that the public safety is threatened by a disabled person going home. Once again, the excesses of cannabis prohibition raise questions with implications that go far beyond the cannabis laws.

In any case, it is now considered likely that Colin will be held in prison until his trial, now set for September.

Colin's supporters demonstrated in front of Strangeways on Saturday, and some of the prison guards told them that they supported the protest because Colin did not belong in prison! Unfortunately, once again there were no newspaper reports on the protest or anything about Colin's ordeal. I am now convinced that the demonstrations should shift to picketing the media. The police and prisons are at least " doing their jobs " even though we don't like it. But the media are definitely not doing their jobs!

As with the prosecution of Scottish MS patient, Ivol, that I reported yesterday, this outrage will hasten the end of cannabis prohibition in the UK, but only if the people are told about it. And that is scant comfort to the victims and their families and friends.
See

The new UK cannabis laws are to be confirmed in Parliament tomorrow and on Thursday MarijuanaNews.com will have a complete analysis of them and the process that brought them about -- and an update on Colin Davies.

There will be no MarijuanaNews posting tomorrow.
